description: The Kubernetes cluster the node belongs to: its API server's endpoint, its address families and ranges, its VIP, the images of its components and the flags of its control-plane components.

allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes.description: Whether workloads run on control-plane nodes, which otherwise register with the taint `node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule`; it is fixed once the node holds a Kubernetes share.

x-chalkos-rules.description: Whether workloads run on control planes stays once the node holds a Kubernetes share.
x-chalkos-rules.message: the config changes allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes; the value applies when the node registers with the cluster, so changing it on a running node changes nothing; add or remove the node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule taint with kubectl taint instead, or reinstall the node

ipv4.description: Service address of the cluster DNS in the family's service range; null is its 10th address. Pods use the primary family's.

ipv6.description: Service address of the cluster DNS in the family's service range; null is its 10th address. Pods use the primary family's.

endpoint.description: URL of the cluster's Kubernetes API server, which every node of the cluster names alike.

etcd.description: Extra flags of etcd, named without the leading dashes with letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, starting with a letter or digit; they override chalkos's own, except the flags chalkos protects, which are refused.

kube-apiserver.description: Extra flags of the API server, named without the leading dashes with letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, starting with a letter or digit; they override chalkos's own, except the flags chalkos protects, which are refused.

kube-controller-manager.description: Extra flags of the controller-manager, named without the leading dashes with letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, starting with a letter or digit; they override chalkos's own, except the flags chalkos protects, which are refused.

kube-scheduler.description: Extra flags of the scheduler, named without the leading dashes with letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, starting with a letter or digit; they override chalkos's own, except the flags chalkos protects, which are refused.

apiServer.description: Image of the API server. containerd pulls it as written: a registry, a repository and a tag, a digest or both. Written as repository:tag@sha256:<digest>, it is pulled by its digest. Its tag is its Kubernetes version, v<major>.<minor>.<patch> with an optional suffix such as -rc.1, which the image's checker compares with the kubelet's and the other components' by Kubernetes's version skew policy.

controllerManager.description: Image of the controller-manager. containerd pulls it as written: a registry, a repository and a tag, a digest or both. Written as repository:tag@sha256:<digest>, it is pulled by its digest. Its tag is its Kubernetes version, v<major>.<minor>.<patch> with an optional suffix such as -rc.1, which the image's checker compares with the kubelet's and the other components' by Kubernetes's version skew policy.

coredns.description: Image of CoreDNS, the cluster DNS. containerd pulls it as written: a registry, a repository and a tag, a digest or both. Written as repository:tag@sha256:<digest>, it is pulled by its digest.

etcd.description: Image of etcd, which control planes run. containerd pulls it as written: a registry, a repository and a tag, a digest or both. Written as repository:tag@sha256:<digest>, it is pulled by its digest.

flannel.description: Image of flannel. containerd pulls it as written: a registry, a repository and a tag, a digest or both. Written as repository:tag@sha256:<digest>, it is pulled by its digest. An image whose CNI is flannel requires it, and an image with another CNI refuses it.

pause.description: Image of the pod sandbox, which containerd runs for every pod. containerd pulls it as written: a registry, a repository and a tag, a digest or both. Written as repository:tag@sha256:<digest>, it is pulled by its digest.

proxy.description: Image of kube-proxy. containerd pulls it as written: a registry, a repository and a tag, a digest or both. Written as repository:tag@sha256:<digest>, it is pulled by its digest. Its tag is its Kubernetes version, v<major>.<minor>.<patch> with an optional suffix such as -rc.1, which the image's checker compares with the kubelet's and the other components' by Kubernetes's version skew policy.

scheduler.description: Image of the scheduler. containerd pulls it as written: a registry, a repository and a tag, a digest or both. Written as repository:tag@sha256:<digest>, it is pulled by its digest. Its tag is its Kubernetes version, v<major>.<minor>.<patch> with an optional suffix such as -rc.1, which the image's checker compares with the kubelet's and the other components' by Kubernetes's version skew policy.

ipFamilies.description: Address families of the cluster, the primary one first, each once. They are fixed when the cluster is created.

x-chalkos-rules.description: The cluster's address families stay once the node holds a Kubernetes share.
x-chalkos-rules.messageExpression: "the config changes the cluster's ipFamilies from " + oldSelf.join(", ") + " to " + self.join(", ") + "; they are fixed once the cluster exists, so keep them, or reinstall the node into a new cluster"

ipv4.description: Prefix length of each node's part of the family's pod range.

ipv6.description: Prefix length of each node's part of the family's pod range.

timeout.description: Seconds a node waits at boot for its address.

validSubnets.description: Subnets in CIDR notation that nodes without a fixed address pick theirs from at boot, unless a Node gives its own; a leading `!` excludes one. Empty takes any global unicast address.

ipv4.description: Address range of the family's pods; each node gets a part of it.

ipv6.description: Address range of the family's pods; each node gets a part of it.

ipv4.description: Address range of the family's services, at most 2^20 addresses.

ipv6.description: Address range of the family's services, at most 2^20 addresses.

addresses.description: Virtual addresses of the API server, at most one per family; empty means no virtual IP.

mode.description: Way the node holding the VIP announces its addresses: `l2` adds them to an interface and announces them to the neighbours with gratuitous ARP and unsolicited neighbour advertisements.

title: Cluster

rules.description: The pod range of each family both configs have stays once the node holds a Kubernetes share.
rules.messageExpression:
cel.bind(was, oldDocuments.map(o, oldDocuments[o].spec)[0], cel.bind(gets, documents.map(n, documents[n].spec)[0], cel.bind(families, was.ipFamilies.filter(f, f in gets.ipFamilies),
  "the config changes the cluster's podCIDRs from "
  + families.map(f, f + " " + string(cidr(was.podCIDRs[f]))).join(", ") + " to "
  + families.map(f, f + " " + string(cidr(gets.podCIDRs[f]))).join(", ") + "; they are fixed once the cluster exists, so keep them, or reinstall the node into a new cluster")
))
rules.rule: facts.share == null || size(oldDocuments) == 0 || size(documents) == 0 || cel.bind(was, oldDocuments.map(o, oldDocuments[o].spec)[0], cel.bind(gets, documents.map(n, documents[n].spec)[0], was.ipFamilies.filter(f, f in gets.ipFamilies).all(f, cidr(was.podCIDRs[f]) == cidr(gets.podCIDRs[f]))))

rules.description: The service range of each family both configs have stays once the node holds a Kubernetes share.
rules.messageExpression:
cel.bind(was, oldDocuments.map(o, oldDocuments[o].spec)[0], cel.bind(gets, documents.map(n, documents[n].spec)[0], cel.bind(families, was.ipFamilies.filter(f, f in gets.ipFamilies),
  "the config changes the cluster's serviceCIDRs from "
  + families.map(f, f + " " + string(cidr(was.serviceCIDRs[f]))).join(", ") + " to "
  + families.map(f, f + " " + string(cidr(gets.serviceCIDRs[f]))).join(", ") + "; they are fixed once the cluster exists, so keep them, or reinstall the node into a new cluster")
))
rules.rule: facts.share == null || size(oldDocuments) == 0 || size(documents) == 0 || cel.bind(was, oldDocuments.map(o, oldDocuments[o].spec)[0], cel.bind(gets, documents.map(n, documents[n].spec)[0], was.ipFamilies.filter(f, f in gets.ipFamilies).all(f, cidr(was.serviceCIDRs[f]) == cidr(gets.serviceCIDRs[f]))))

rules.description: The cluster DNS's address of each family both configs have, by default the 10th of its service range, stays once the node holds a Kubernetes share.
rules.messageExpression:
cel.bind(was, oldDocuments.map(o, oldDocuments[o].spec)[0], cel.bind(gets, documents.map(n, documents[n].spec)[0], cel.bind(families, was.ipFamilies.filter(f, f in gets.ipFamilies),
  "the config changes the cluster's dnsIPs from "
  + families.map(f, f + " " + string((was.dnsIPs[f] != null ? ip(was.dnsIPs[f]) : cidr(was.serviceCIDRs[f]).ip(10)))).join(", ") + " to "
  + families.map(f, f + " " + string((gets.dnsIPs[f] != null ? ip(gets.dnsIPs[f]) : cidr(gets.serviceCIDRs[f]).ip(10)))).join(", ") + "; they are fixed once the cluster exists, so keep them, or reinstall the node into a new cluster")
))
rules.rule: facts.share == null || size(oldDocuments) == 0 || size(documents) == 0 || cel.bind(was, oldDocuments.map(o, oldDocuments[o].spec)[0], cel.bind(gets, documents.map(n, documents[n].spec)[0], was.ipFamilies.filter(f, f in gets.ipFamilies).all(f, (was.dnsIPs[f] != null ? ip(was.dnsIPs[f]) : cidr(was.serviceCIDRs[f]).ip(10)) == (gets.dnsIPs[f] != null ? ip(gets.dnsIPs[f]) : cidr(gets.serviceCIDRs[f]).ip(10)))))
